back: Used for an activity in progress before a particular point in the past.
Simple for achievement (worked her way up); continuous for duration (working for months).
Either simple or continuous can be used (e.g., 'had been looking forward').
Use past perfect simple for states or long-held beliefs.
Past perfect simple focuses on the specific result of an action.

front: Ex 7.1 (1a): She ... for the company for months.
Ex 7.1 (1b): She ... her way up to management.
Ex 7.1 (2b): She ... a bottle from the bag.
Ex 7.1 (3b): She ... for jobs without success.
Ex 7.1 (4a): He ... from NY for the meeting.

back: It was the third time I had arrived late.
They had been complaining of a headache most of yesterday.
